subject: Capital Stabilization Fund Infrastructure Appropriations
overview: The committee reviewed and referred several requests to appropriate money from the Capital Stabilization Fund for school equipment, roadway repairs, and facility maintenance. The administration also addressed concerns regarding the impact of the upcoming override vote on labor negotiations.

items.title: Capital Stabilization Fund Appropriation Request (24-473)
items.summary: Referred a request for $614,728 in various appropriations to the regular meeting for further action.

items.title: Brooks Elementary Water Heater Replacement
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Peter Cushing explained that the failed original unit will be replaced with a high-efficiency gas model because full electrification costs were prohibitively high.

items.title: Roadway Patching
items.summary: City Engineer Owen Wartella detailed the need for additional funding to cover a nearly 25 percent increase in asphalt costs since spring estimates were prepared.

items.title: Parking Lot Light Pole Replacement
items.summary: Superintendent of Wires Steve Randazzo recommended replacing 40-year-old light poles in municipal lots after a pole collapsed due to advanced deterioration.

items.title: City Hall Elevator Repairs
items.summary: Facilities Director Paul Righi reported that unforeseen electrical and fire alarm code upgrades extended the repair timeline and increased costs.

items.title: Brooks Estate Repairs
items.summary: Land Trust President Carly Nessen requested funding for roof repairs and winterization to preserve the manor and prepare for new caretakers.

items.title: Discussion on Labor Negotiations
items.summary: Councilor Scarpelli raised reports of police contract negotiations being delayed due to the upcoming override vote; Chief of Staff Nina Nazarian stated the administration has not delayed any negotiations.
